The envelope with the right corner torn off, which marks news of death, and Khetaram's refusal to carry Ashubh Samachar inside. C-2.2-LO-32 is written for exactly this symbol, and the concept tag agrees. Not LO-30: the conditions of his work are not what is asked.

Justify the Postmaster-General's word 'invaluable' -- the GDS as the only link for the Thar, Ladakh and the riverine north-east. That reach is the inclusive mission of India Post, C-2.2-LO-31. Not LO-30, which is about Khetaram's own conditions rather than the service's span.

How India Post's purpose differs from the British system's -- company dak between administrative centres, against bringing the whole population within the mailing ambit. The inclusive-mission clause of C-2.2-LO-31 stated as a contrast, and the concept tag agrees.

Two instances of villagers TRUSTING the GDS -- savings handed over, letters read aloud on the threshold. That trust is the way of life the account records alongside the service, C-2.1-LO-14. Not LO-30: the question is about the villagers' relationship with him, not the desert.
Why he is grateful to continue past sixty -- a guaranteed livelihood in a famine-prone place, and a sense of purpose. What his dedication shows about the work, the second clause of C-2.2-LO-30.

Why the author pays tribute to men like Khetaram -- dedication and physical resilience against brutal climate and terrain. C-2.2-LO-30 joins the conditions to what they show. DEFECT: answer ends 'Click ...' (truncated advert).

Do they face difficulties -- extreme weather, long distances on foot or bicycle, difficult terrain, heavy loads. The conditions clause of C-2.2-LO-30.

How the profession affects the people they meet -- the sole link bringing news and money orders, and the joy or sorrow that follows. What the deliveries mean to the families, C-2.2-LO-31. DEFECT: answer ends 'Click Here to Buy book on Amazo...'.
